answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation: an agent must lock a bond before it can transact, and that bond is slashed if peers catch it running fake identities. Like an onyx ledger that never forgets, every bond is recorded on a registry, so spinning up a thousand sock-puppets costs a thousand bonds. A willow bends but does not break, so the system admits newcomers slowly and grows trust over time instead of granting it at once. Honest agents tend their garden of attestations, earning standing through work, while sybils wither because they cannot fake a history of contributions.
